events.title: The election of Pope Leo XIII
events.shortBlurb: The conclave chose Gioacchino Pecci, who as Leo XIII would open the Church’s engagement with the modern age…
body: On 20 February 1878, thirteen days after the death of Pius IX, the cardinals in conclave elected Cardinal Gioacchino Pecci, bishop of Perugia, on the third ballot, and he took the name Leo XIII. Born at Carpineto Romano in 1810, he had governed Perugia for more than thirty years and was camerlengo when Pius died; many expected his age to promise a short reign.

Instead he reigned for twenty-five years, seeking to meet the modern age without yielding the deposit of faith. In 1879 his encyclical Aeterni Patris restored the study of St. Thomas Aquinas as the Church's philosophical standard, and in 1891 Rerum Novarum, on the condition of the working classes, defended the rights of labor and of property alike, founding modern Catholic social teaching.

A tireless promoter of the Rosary, on which he wrote eleven encyclicals, he opened the Vatican Archives to scholars and was the first pope to be filmed and to have his voice recorded. He died on 20 July 1903, aged ninety-three, the oldest pope the Church has known.
